title: Namecheap Hosting Review 2026: Shared vs EasyWP Plans
excerpt: Namecheap Stellar is $2.28 a month on a yearly plan and renews at $55.88 a year. Here is how shared hosting and EasyWP compare, what each costs, how fast they tested and who should look elsewhere.

meta._yoast_wpseo_title: Namecheap Hosting Review 2026: Shared vs EasyWP Plans
meta._yoast_wpseo_metadesc: Namecheap hosting review for 2026: shared hosting versus EasyWP plans, prices and renewals, WordPress support and who each plan suits, with setup steps.
meta.rl_answer: Namecheap has two WordPress routes: shared hosting for several sites and EasyWP for one managed site. Stellar is $2.28 a month billed yearly and renews at $55.88 a year.
meta.rl_faqs:
Is Namecheap hosting good? | Yes for small sites on a budget. Independent tests measured 99.95% to 99.98% uptime and 232 to 462 ms time to first byte in the US. Visitors far from its servers see slower responses.
Is Namecheap hosting good for WordPress? | Yes, on either route. Shared hosting installs WordPress with Softaculous in cPanel. EasyWP is a managed WordPress plan with a simpler dashboard. Shared hosting runs on Apache, which trails LiteSpeed hosts on first-byte time.
Does Namecheap host websites? | Yes. Namecheap sells shared hosting (Stellar, Stellar Plus and Stellar Business), EasyWP managed WordPress, VPS and dedicated servers, and it is also a domain registrar.
Does Namecheap hosting have WordPress? | Yes. On shared hosting you install WordPress with Softaculous in cPanel. On EasyWP, WordPress is set up for you when you create the site.
Can I use WordPress on shared hosting at Namecheap? | Yes. Shared hosting supports WordPress and other systems such as Joomla and Drupal, plus custom PHP and HTML sites. Stellar allows 3 websites, and Stellar Plus and Business allow unlimited.
Can you get WordPress hosting for free at Namecheap? | Not permanently. Namecheap offers a free 30-day trial on shared hosting, and WPThinker says EasyWP Starter has a free first month on monthly billing. After that you pay.
Does Namecheap offer a free trial? | Namecheap lists a free 30-day trial on shared hosting, according to WPThinker and BearHost. WPThinker says the 30-day money-back guarantee does not apply if you started with the trial, so read the terms.
How much does Namecheap hosting cost? | On Namecheap's pages on 20 November 2026, Stellar was $2.28 a month billed yearly, Stellar Plus $2.98 and Stellar Business $4.98. EasyWP Starter was $1.48 in the sale. The sale ends 4 December 2026.
How much does Namecheap hosting cost after renewal? | Stellar renews at $55.88 a year, about $4.66 a month. Stellar Plus renews at $85.44 and Stellar Business at $128.88 a year. EasyWP Starter renews at $68.88 a year.
What is the difference between EasyWP and shared hosting? | EasyWP hosts one WordPress site per plan on a cloud platform with its own dashboard. Shared hosting uses cPanel, hosts several sites and includes email. Namecheap's help article lists the details.
Does EasyWP have automatic backups? | The sources disagree. Namecheap's help article lists website backups among the features, and WPThinker lists automatic backups. HostingStep reported none on Starter in its 2026 test. Check the backup option in your dashboard.
Is Namecheap good for beginners? | Yes. Both routes have simple setup, and Namecheap keeps your domain and hosting in one account. Shared hosting uses cPanel, which takes a little learning.
Does Namecheap include email with hosting? | Shared hosting does. Stellar includes 30 mailboxes, and Stellar Plus and Business include unlimited. EasyWP does not bundle email on every plan, so you may need a separate email service.

meta.rl_takeaways:
Stellar is $2.28 a month billed yearly and renews at $55.88 a year, about $4.66 a month (Namecheap, 20 Nov 2026).
EasyWP Starter is $1.48 a month billed yearly in the sale and renews at $68.88 a year. The sale ends 4 Dec 2026.
Shared hosting hosts several sites and includes email. EasyWP hosts one site per plan.
Independent tests found fast US responses and slower ones in Asia.
meta.rl_r_verdict: Namecheap is a good low-cost home for small WordPress sites, especially if you want your domain and email in one account. Choose shared hosting for several sites and EasyWP for one managed site, read the renewal price, and use the 30-day window to test it.
meta.rl_r_buy:
You want a low price and your domain and hosting in one account.
You need email included (shared hosting) or one managed WordPress site (EasyWP).
Most of your visitors are in the US or Europe.
meta.rl_r_skip:
Most of your visitors are in Asia or far from its servers.
You want LiteSpeed speed.
You want daily backups on a budget plan.
meta.rl_r_pros:
Low first-year prices and a smaller renewal jump than many hosts.
Two routes: shared hosting for several sites and EasyWP for one.
Email included on shared hosting.
100% uptime promise on shared hosting and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
Domains and hosting in one account.
meta.rl_r_cons:
Apache shared hosting trails LiteSpeed hosts.
Slower for far-away visitors.
EasyWP hosts one site per plan.
Twice-a-week backups on shared plans.
Sources disagree on EasyWP backups.

meta.rl_r_method:
Our own use | We do not host our own site on Namecheap, so this is a research-based review. We did not run our own tests
Pricing and plan limits | Namecheap's shared hosting page, EasyWP pricing page and help article, read on 20 November 2026. We recorded each plan price, the term it needs, the renewal price and the limits
Independent tests | HostingStep (October 2025 to May 2026), HostingGuider (May 2026) and TopSiteHosters (April 2026)
Competitor reviews | The top-ranking Namecheap reviews read for structure and questions: WPThinker, BearHost, HostingGuider, TopSiteHosters and WebHostWatch
Questions people ask | The questions the top pages answer in their headings, plus the questions people search for in Semrush, such as whether Namecheap hosting is good for WordPress and what EasyWP costs
When sources disagree | We show both views and say which we used. For EasyWP backups the sources disagree, so we say so
Our calculations | The five-year cost table is our own arithmetic from Namecheap's prices
Freshness | Prices and offers are read again before this page goes live, and the page carries the date they were checked
What we did not do | We did not run our own speed or uptime test. Each test number is credited to the team that measured it
